summary: A single real Ausca browser.session invocation paid USD 0.05 over x402 on Base, returned a ready 600-second lease, loaded https://example.com/ through one CDP connection with title 'Example Domain', and was explicitly closed with an authoritative closed-state readback.

receipt.page_statement: Ausca published a delivery receipt: Ausca Browser Session completed.

observations.actual: GET /v1/offers/browser.session returned revision browser-duration-r3 and all three frozen digests; Frantic #134 was funded/open with 7 of 10 slots available; agent-904bdb was eligible with zero active claims; the required GitHub star returned HTTP 204.

POST /v1/invocations/prepare returned paid_b68d9f17-4475-405c-9f57-38cbc6bacdbb and an x402 v2 quote; the exact 448-byte envelope then returned unsigned HTTP 402 with Base USDC amount 50000 and payTo 0x26572ff23c6c52bfb1a69cb0c9114a8be443b422.

After the single Frantic claim was created, the unchanged envelope was sent once with a host-held PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Settlement took 9304 ms and returned success=true for payer 0xA29D08d14eC2614B29cf06d5ee59a1bB710b4366 in transaction 0x617ee320c9550acdbe5aafaed46bcb592e36667e0d9f835b7ce5427021fba2e1.

The paid POST returned HTTP 200 synchronously with status=accepted and invocation.state=succeeded. The body had inspect_url, invocation, resource_access, and status; the public readback preserved output_digest sha256:72675ed60dbcd73dd9f7239ddd6a616af9c9b8efad5983af657eab22c8ea9c55.
No terminal polling was required: poll_count=0 because the first paid response was already succeeded; no replay and no second payment identity were used.

The lease status was ready, one connection ticket was minted, one CDP connection loaded https://example.com/ with HTTP 200 and title 'Example Domain', then DELETE returned status=closed and a final authenticated GET returned state=closed.

The public invocation exposed a runx receipt URL that returned HTTP 200 and stated that Ausca Browser Session completed. Its HTML did not expose the settled amount or transaction, and its advertised application/json alternate returned HTTP 404; the Base explorer independently showed the successful 0.05 USDC transfer.

The successful-run timeline began at 2026-09-19T19:56:15.669Z and ended at 2026-09-19T19:56:44.293Z. The invocation succeeded, CDP proof completed, lease closed, and public receipt appeared inside that interval.

issues.finding: The bounty text says to preserve a canonicalizer, but the live Ausca OpenAPI InvocationEnvelope has no canonicalizer property and sets additionalProperties=false. I followed the machine schema and preserved the revision, three digests, input, and idempotency key instead.

The live exact/Base/USDC requirement omitted assetTransferMethod, so @x402/evm had to use its backward-compatible EIP-3009 default. The payment succeeded, but the transfer method was inferred rather than explicit in the challenge.

The endpoint returned status=connected while it had only minted a single-use WebSocket ticket; the actual CDP handshake happened afterward. A status such as ticket_issued would distinguish issuance from a live connection.

The receipt HTML advertised this application/json alternate, but the alternate returned HTTP 404. The HTML also omitted the USD 0.05 amount and transaction hash that the bounty asks a reviewer to confirm.

proposed_improvement.change: Make the advertised receipt JSON endpoint return a stable public document containing the non-secret service id, settled amount, network, transaction hash, and completion time, and render those same fields on the receipt page. This would let a stranger complete the review from receipt_ref alone instead of combining Ausca readback with a chain explorer.
